sources.entry: elasticsearch - The official low-level Python client for Elasticsearch.

summary.one_liner: The official low-level Python client for Elasticsearch, used to connect to clusters and index, search, update and delete documents from Python code.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a client that translates basic Python data types to and from JSON and handles cluster connections. It lists configurable discovery of cluster nodes, persistent connections, and load balancing across nodes with a pluggable selection strategy. Failed connections are penalized on a time basis and not retried until a timeout passes. It supports TLS and HTTP authentication, is thread-safe across requests, and includes helper functions for using APIs together. The usage section lists the basic operations: creating and deleting an index, indexing, getting, searching and updating documents. The README does not include code examples, so the exact API surface is documented elsewhere.
use_cases: connect a Python app to an Elasticsearch cluster
index and search documents from Python
update or delete documents in Elasticsearch
balance requests across multiple Elasticsearch nodes
how_to_run: Refer to the Installation section of the getting started documentation (README does not give install commands)
Refer to the Connecting section of the getting started documentation
Optional: run Elasticsearch and Kibana locally using the curl | sh command in the README
notable: Automatic node discovery and load balancing with a pluggable selection strategy
Forward compatible with equivalent and later minor Elasticsearch versions
Older client versions published as elasticsearch7 and elasticsearch8
caveats: README defers installation, connection setup and documentation links to external docs; the links are empty in this copy
New Elasticsearch features are only supported in the matching client version
